In
enzymology
, a
(+)-neomenthol dehydrogenase
(
EC
1.1.1.208
) is an
enzyme
that
catalyzes
the
chemical reaction
(+)-neomenthol
+
NADP
+
H
+
H
+
(–)-menthone
+
NADPH
The two
substrates
of this enzyme are (+)-neomenthol and oxidised
nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate
(NADP
+
). Its
products
are (−)-menthone, reduced NADPH, and a
proton
.
[
1
]
[
2
]
This enzyme belongs to the family of
oxidoreductases
, specifically those acting on the CH-OH group of donor with NAD
+
or NADP
+
as acceptor. The
systematic name
of this enzyme class is
(+)-neomenthol:NADP
+
oxidoreductase
. This enzyme is also called
monoterpenoid dehydrogenase
. This enzyme participates in
monoterpenoid
biosynthesis.
See also
(−)-menthol dehydrogenase
